1→//! Error pattern registry for step failure recovery.
     2→//!
     3→//! Matches step failure output against known patterns to suggest fixes.
     4→//! Patterns have confidence levels: `High` confidence matches produce
     5→//! actionable Fix options in the recovery menu, while `Low` confidence
     6→//! matches produce hints below the error block.
     7→
     8→use regex::Regex;
     9→use std::sync::LazyLock;
    10→
    11→/// Confidence level for a pattern match.
    12→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
    13→pub enum Confidence {
    14→    /// Strong pattern match — show as an actionable Fix option in the menu.
    15→    High,
    16→    /// Weaker match — show as a hint below the error block only.
    17→    Low,
    18→}
    19→
    20→/// A suggested fix command for a recognized error.
    21→#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
    22→pub struct FixSuggestion {
    23→    /// Shown in menu (e.g., "bundle update nokogiri").
    24→    pub label: String,
    25→    /// Command to actually run.
    26→    pub command: String,
    27→    /// Why this fix is suggested.
    28→    pub explanation: String,
    29→    /// How confident the match is.
    30→    pub confidence: Confidence,
    31→}
    32→
    33→/// Context about the step that failed, used for pattern filtering.
    34→pub struct StepContext<'a> {
    35→    /// Step name.
    36→    pub name: &'a str,
    37→    /// Step command.
    38→    pub command: &'a str,
    39→    /// Step requirements (e.g., ["postgres-server", "ruby"]).
    40→    pub requires: &'a [String],
    41→    /// Template name, if any.
    42→    pub template: Option<&'a str>,
    43→}
    44→
    45→/// Controls when a pattern fires.
    46→#[derive(Debug)]
    47→pub enum PatternContext {
    48→    /// Fires for any step.
    49→    Always,
    50→    /// Only fires if the step command contains this substring.
    51→    CommandContains(&'static str),
    52→    /// Only fires if the step requires one of these.
    53→    RequiresAny(&'static [&'static str]),
    54→}
    55→
    56→impl PatternContext {
    57→    fn matches(&self, ctx: &StepContext) -> bool {
    58→        match self {
    59→            PatternContext::Always => true,
    60→            PatternContext::CommandContains(substr) => {
    61→                // Support pipe-separated alternatives: "pip|python"
    62→                substr.split('|').any(|s| ctx.command.contains(s))
    63→            }
    64→            PatternContext::RequiresAny(reqs) => {
    65→                reqs.iter().any(|r| ctx.requires.iter().any(|s| s == r))
    66→            }
    67→        }
    68→    }
    69→}
    70→
    71→/// A registered error pattern.
    72→pub struct ErrorPattern {
    73→    /// Pattern name (for debugging).
    74→    pub name: &'static str,
    75→    /// Regex to match against error output.
    76→    pub regex: &'static str,
    77→    /// When this pattern fires.
    78→    pub context: PatternContext,
    79→    /// Confidence level.
    80→    pub confidence: Confidence,

    20→/// Regex for scrubbing filesystem paths.

    78→/// Scrub sensitive data from text for telemetry.
    79→///
    80→/// 1. Masks known secret env var values using `OutputMasker`
    81→/// 2. Replaces filesystem paths with `[PATH]`
    82→/// 3. Replaces token-like strings with `[REDACTED]`
    83→/// 4. Truncates to `MAX_ERROR_LENGTH` chars
    84→pub fn scrub_for_telemetry(input: &str, step_env: &HashMap<String, String>) -> String {
    85→    let matcher = SecretMatcher::with_builtins();
    86→    let mut masker = OutputMasker::new();
    87→
    88→    // Mask known secret env var values
    89→    for (key, value) in step_env {
    90→        if matcher.is_secret(key) && !value.is_empty() {
    91→            masker.add_secret(value);
    92→        }
    93→    }
    94→
    95→    let mut result = masker.mask(input);
    96→
    97→    // Scrub filesystem paths
    98→    result = PATH_REGEX.replace_all(&result, "[PATH]").to_string();
    99→
   100→    // Scrub token-like strings
   101→    result = TOKEN_REGEX.replace_all(&result, "[REDACTED]").to_string();
   102→
   103→    // Truncate
   104→    if result.len() > MAX_ERROR_LENGTH {
   105→        result.truncate(MAX_ERROR_LENGTH);
   106→        result.push_str("...[truncated]");
   107→    }
   108→
   109→    result
   110→}

   112→/// Build a `FailureReport` from step failure context.
   113→pub fn build_report(

   125→        command_scrubbed: scrub_for_telemetry(command, step_env),
   126→        exit_code,

   128→        recovery_action: recovery_action.to_string(),

   134→/// Prompt the user for telemetry consent after a successful recovery.
   135→///
   136→/// Returns `None` if the preference is already saved (always/never).
   137→/// Checks `preferences_other` for the `telemetry_failures` key.
   138→pub fn prompt_telemetry(
   139→    ui: &mut dyn UserInterface,

   149→
   150→    // Show the scrubbed report to the user
   151→    ui.message("");
   152→    ui.message("  Help bivvy get smarter?");
   153→    ui.message("  We'd save this failure report to improve auto-recovery:");
   154→    ui.message("");
   155→    ui.message(&format!("    Step:    {}", report.step_name));
   156→    ui.message(&format!("    Command: {}", report.command_scrubbed));
   157→    if let Some(code) = report.exit_code {
   158→        ui.message(&format!("    Exit:    {}", code));
   159→    }
   160→    if !report.error_scrubbed.is_empty() {
   161→        ui.message(&format!("    Error:   {}", report.error_scrubbed));
   162→    }
   163→    ui.message(&format!("    Fix:     {}", report.recovery_action));
   164→    ui.message("");
   165→    ui.message("    NO env vars, paths, secrets, or project code — just the above.");
   166→    ui.message("");
   167→
   168→    let prompt = Prompt {
   169→        key: "telemetry_failure".to_string(),
   170→        question: "Save this failure report?".to_string(),
   171→        prompt_type: PromptType::Select {
   172→            options: vec![
   173→                PromptOption {
   174→                    label: "Send".to_string(),
   175→                    value: "send".to_string(),
   176→                },
   177→                PromptOption {
   178→                    label: "No thanks".to_string(),
   179→                    value: "no_thanks".to_string(),
   180→                },
   181→                PromptOption {
   182→                    label: "Always send".to_string(),
   183→                    value: "always".to_string(),
   184→                },
   185→                PromptOption {
   186→                    label: "Never ask".to_string(),
   187→                    value: "never".to_string(),
   188→                },
   189→            ],
   190→        },
   191→        default: Some("no_thanks".to_string()),
   192→    };

   194→    let answer = ui.prompt(&prompt)?;

   201→}

   218→/// Save a failure report to a specific directory (for testing).
   219→pub fn save_report_to(report: &FailureReport, dir: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
   220→    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
   221→
   222→    let timestamp = chrono::Utc::now().format("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S");
   223→    let filename = format!("{}-{}.yml", timestamp, report.step_name);
   224→    let path = dir.join(filename);
   225→
   226→    let content = serde_yaml::to_string(report).map_err(|e| {
   227→        crate::error::BivvyError::ConfigValidationError {
   228→            message: format!("Failed to serialize failure report: {}", e),
   229→        }
   230→    })?;
   231→
   232→    std::fs::write(&path, content)?;
   233→    Ok(path)
   234→}
